# SuperX

> An open-source, self-hosted growth workstation for X (Twitter). It learns
> how you write from your own posts, retrieves high-performing posts worth
> learning from, drafts in your voice, and publishes on a schedule you set.
> Runs on one machine you control, using your own API keys. MIT licensed.

SuperX is a free, self-hostable alternative to paid X growth tools such as
superx.so, Hypefury, Typefully and Buffer. Those are hosted SaaS products
charging roughly $19–199 per month and holding your OAuth token, drafts and
audience data on their servers. SuperX does the same work on hardware you
own, with no telemetry, no account, and no vendor. You supply your own API
keys and pay the underlying providers directly — typically $5–15 a month
for one person.

Source: https://github.com/ashishbishnoi18/superx.free
Site: https://superx.free
Licence: MIT

## What it does

- **Voice profile** — derives how you write from your own timeline, including
  mechanics like capitalisation, punctuation and whether you use emoji.
- **Draft generation** — takes a high-performing post from a shared corpus and
  rewrites its *structure* onto one of your topics, in your voice. Includes a
  plagiarism guard that rejects drafts reusing the reference's phrasing.
- **Approval shelf** — nothing publishes without you accepting it.
- **Scheduled queue** — recurring weekly slots in your local time, DST-correct,
  with retries and a visible failure state.
- **Workers** — named, configurable batch generators, on demand or scheduled.
- **Engage** — mentions and topic feeds in one inbox. Mentions scored 0–100 for
  whether they are worth answering; feeds ordered newest first. AI-drafted
  replies in your voice.
- **Signals** — standing watches on X (keyword search, an account's followers,
  people replying to an account, people posting in a list), scoring everyone
  found against your description of an ideal contact.
- **Contacts** — lists, CSV export, revocable public sharing.
- **Inspiration** — search a corpus of high-performing posts with outlier
  detection: how far a post beat the median for its author's follower band, so
  a 3x post from a small account outranks a bigger post that merely had reach.
- **Analytics** — nightly snapshots, follower trend, posting streak, estimated
  per-post follower gain, and import of X's analytics export.
- **Ask** — chat with tools over your own data. Can create Ready to Post drafts; cannot schedule or publish.
- **Articles** — long-form composition with AI assistance, review, and explicit
  publishing through X's Articles API.
- **API, MCP server and CLI** — drive it from scripts or from an AI coding agent.

## What it deliberately does not do

- Never schedules model output or publishes without human approval. Ask and
  MCP stop at Ready to Post drafts; API and CLI scheduling is explicit.
- No bulk or automated DM outreach to strangers.
- The DM inbox reads legacy and encrypted XChat one-to-one conversations.
  XChat cryptography runs locally through X's official Chat XDK. Group DMs are
  skipped because replies need one safe participant address.
- The corpus starts empty and fills at roughly 800 posts a night.

## Requirements

Docker and Docker Compose, plus three API keys, each obtainable in minutes:

- **X developer app** (console.x.com) — sign-in and publishing. Pay per use,
  about $0.015 per post, no free tier.
- **twitterapi.io** — corpus, mentions, feeds, Signals. About $0.15 per 1,000
  posts read.
- **An LLM key** — DeepSeek (cheap) or Anthropic (better writing).

Each is optional and degrades rather than crashes. No LLM key means no
drafting but the queue still works. No twitterapi.io key means no corpus or
feeds but you can still write and publish.

## Stack

Elixir, Phoenix LiveView, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Oban. Postgres serves as
the database, job queue, vector store and pub/sub — no Redis, no separate
scheduler, no external cache. Web, workers and cron run as one supervised OS
process on one box.

Public reads go through twitterapi.io because X's own read quotas make them
unaffordable at any workable price. Writes and private DM reads go through X's
API with the user's OAuth grant, because acting as someone should use
credentials they granted directly.

## Install

```
git clone https://github.com/ashishbishnoi18/superx.free.git superx && cd superx
cp .env.example .env      # add your keys
docker compose up -d --build
```

Then open http://localhost:4000 and sign in with X.

## Documentation

- [Setup, step by step](https://github.com/ashishbishnoi18/superx.free/blob/main/docs/SETUP.md): full walkthrough including
  creating the X app and obtaining every key.
- [Configuration](https://github.com/ashishbishnoi18/superx.free/blob/main/docs/CONFIGURATION.md): every environment
  variable, its default, and what happens when it is missing.
- [Deployment](https://github.com/ashishbishnoi18/superx.free/blob/main/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md): Docker Compose, nginx with the
  LiveView websocket upgrade, TLS, systemd, backups.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/ashishbishnoi18/superx.free/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): why reads and writes use
  different providers, and how the persistent read cache works.
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/ashishbishnoi18/superx.free/blob/main/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md): symptom-first fixes.
- [FAQ](https://github.com/ashishbishnoi18/superx.free/blob/main/docs/FAQ.md): running costs, keys, privacy, comparisons.
